title: Module 1 Quiz — Containers & the app image

questions.prompt: If someone edited apps/common/views.py and rebuilt this image, which stages would need to re-run their layers, and which would hit cache? Walk through it stage by stage.
questions.rubric: Should identify that builder/builder-dev wheel-building stages are cache-hit (unaffected by app code changes since they only depend on requirements files), while runtime's COPY . . layer and everything after it in that stage must re-run because the app source changed. Full credit requires naming the specific COPY that invalidates and explaining why requirements-only stages are unaffected.

questions.prompt: A teammate 'simplifies' the Dockerfile by deleting the builder stage and running apt-get install gcc ... && pip install -r requirements/prod.txt directly in a single stage. Name two concrete costs: one about image size/attack surface, one about build speed on repeated builds.
questions.rubric: Attack surface: compiler toolchain (gcc etc.) now ships in the production image, larger attack surface if the container is compromised. Build speed: without the two-stage split, any app code change forces re-running the full apt-get + pip install + compile step since there's no separate cacheable dependency layer isolated from source copies.

questions.prompt: The runtime stage does COPY . . after installing dependencies from wheels. Why is that order correct given layer caching? What would break/slow down if flipped?
questions.rubric: Correct order keeps the expensive dependency install layer cached across source-only changes. Flipping it means COPY . . (which changes on every commit) would sit before the pip install layer, invalidating the dependency install cache on every single code change — every build reinstalls all dependencies from scratch.

questions.prompt: The development stage temporarily switches to USER root, installs dev wheels, then switches back to USER appuser. Why can't it stay as appuser for the whole stage?
questions.rubric: appuser lacks filesystem permissions to install packages into system site-packages / write to protected paths; pip install would fail with a permissions error without root.

questions.prompt: The production stage's CMD is /start-api.sh, but the same image also runs the Celery worker and beat. How does that actually happen, given the image only has one CMD?
questions.rubric: Compose services override the image's default CMD per-service via the `command:` key (e.g. ["/start-worker.sh"], ["/start-beat.sh"]) — the image itself is generic; the specific process it runs is decided at container-start time by Compose, not baked into the image.
